content_voiceover: Extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma, nasal type, has a distinctive morphology, immunophenotype, and clinical course that boards love to test. Morphologically, about a third of cases show tumor cells invading blood vessels, which is why it's also called angiocentric NK/T cell lymphoma. The immunophenotype is CD2 positive, surface CD3 negative but cytoplasmic CD3 positive, CD5 negative, CD7 negative, CD4 negative, CD8 negative, CD16 positive, CD56 positive, CD45RO positive, and TIA-1 positive, and critically there is usually no TCR gene rearrangement, confirming its NK cell, rather than T cell, origin in most cases. Molecularly, it is almost universally associated with Epstein-Barr virus. Epidemiologically, it's far more common in Asia, particularly Taiwan, Hong Kong, Korea, mainland China, and Japan, accounting for five to ten percent of lymphomas there, while it's rare in Western populations. Typical age at diagnosis is thirty to fifty, averaging around forty, with a slight male predominance. Clinically it involves midline upper respiratory structures, the nose, palate, pharynx, and nasopharynx, with nodal involvement in less than ten percent, which is why it's classically called midline lethal granuloma. At autopsy, extensive sinus invasion and even brain invasion can be seen, which makes radiation planning and staging difficult. It can extend to skin and the GI tract causing ulceration and bleeding, and bone marrow involvement, seen in five to ten percent, can trigger hemophagocytic syndrome and rapid death. It responds poorly to chemotherapy alone; early stage disease can be well controlled with radiotherapy, achieving five year survival of fifty to sixty percent, but disseminated disease carries a very poor prognosis.
keypoints: Angiocentric NK/T cell lymphoma; surface CD3 negative, cytoplasmic CD3 positive, CD56 positive, no TCR rearrangement
Much more common in Asia; median age around 40
Midline destructive lesion of nose/palate/pharynx, historically called midline lethal granuloma
Bone marrow involvement can trigger hemophagocytic syndrome and rapid death; poor response to chemo alone
keypoint_voiceover: High yield points: this is a CD3 surface negative, CD56 positive, EBV driven NK cell lymphoma with no TCR gene rearrangement, classically causing midline destructive nasal disease. It's Asia predominant, responds poorly to chemotherapy alone, but early stage disease does well with radiotherapy. Watch for hemophagocytic syndrome if bone marrow is involved.
